messages:
maria-cs: Heads up — Acme reconciliation returning odd numbers during EOM. Dashboard shows 28,134 total tokens for April but invoice INV-2026-04-ACME that just posted is for 35,210 tokens. Customer emailed escalation. Can someone triage? :eyes:
ben-ops: Do we have account_id and billing window?
maria-cs: account acme-corp (acct_42). Window is 2026-04-01 00:00:00 to 2026-04-30 23:59:59 UTC. Invoice posted at 2026-05-01T06:02:12Z. Customer says dashboard always matched invoice before.
raj-billing: Reproducing locally — quick check of raw_metering for acct_42: ran query against metering.ledger_snapshot_v2 for 2026-04 and got ~35,200 tokens.
raj-billing: SQL snippet: ```SELECT sum(tokens) FROM metering.events WHERE acct_id='acct_42' AND timestamp >= '2026-04-01' AND timestamp < '2026-05-01';```
alisa-sre: Hmm, dashboard aggregate service uses the daily-aggregator job which writes to dashboard_rollups table. I see a retry/backfill for 2026-04-30 at 2026-05-01T02:50Z in the orchestrator logs — maybe timing mismatch with invoice snapshot.
maria-cs: dashboard UI is showing 28,134 though — can we export the dashboard rollup for that account and diff against ledger? Customer screenshot attached in email: shows 28,134 in UI.
ben-ops: I'll pull the dashboard_rollups rows. ```SELECT date, tokens_rollup FROM dashboard_rollups WHERE acct_id='acct_42' AND date >= '2026-04-01' AND date <= '2026-04-30' ORDER BY date;```
ben-ops: Quick grep shows a gap on 2026-04-28 -> no row for that date between 00:00-01:00 UTC. That date had a late ingestion for a legacy pipeline.
raj-billing: Could be a legacy-plan mapping problem. Acme was on legacy 'priority_plus' plan until 2026-04-15 and then migrated to 'priority' tier. Our invoice meter maps legacy plan_code differently, and credits/prorations run in the billing job. If ledger includes both migrated usage and leftover legacy credits, invoice might count extra tokens due to plan_code double-count.
ken-finance: Can you paste the invoice line items? I want to see plan tiers and proration credits.
maria-cs: Invoice snippet (sanitized): 
```
Invoice ID: INV-2026-04-ACME
Lines:
  - PLAN_PRIORITY - 25,000 tokens - $250.00
  - USAGE_OVERAGE - 10,210 tokens - $102.10
  - CREDIT_PRORATE - -0 tokens - -$0.00
Total tokens shown: 35,210
```
ben-ops: Dashboard rollup export (sum of daily tokens): 28,134. I can see a missing upload on 2026-04-28 and 2026-04-29 had partial values — aggregator job crashed on 04-28 23:45 UTC due to upstream S3 timeout. We retried but the dashboard writer skipped duplicate idempotency checks because the legacy pipeline uses a different event_id format.
raj-billing: So ledger (used for bill calc) got all raw events directly from raw_metering stream (kafka), but dashboard_rollups missed a batch due to the S3->ingest path failure. That explains invoice > dashboard.
alisa-sre: Confirmed in logs: ```[2026-04-28T23:44:57Z] aggregator ERROR failed to fetch s3://events-archive/2026-04-28/batch-334.json -> 504```. Retry succeeded later but with new event_ids that dashboard writer filtered as duplicates. Old writer only deduped by event_id for the legacy format. New events had canonical ids and were stored to ledger but not counted in dashboard_rollups.
ken-finance: Is there an easy way to recompute the dashboard totals so customer sees matching numbers? Or should we reissue invoice?
raj-billing: We should recompute dashboard_rollups for acct_42 for the affected dates and re-run the UI cache. Also need to consider if invoice is correct — ledger is source-of-truth for billing, so invoice is likely accurate. But we can recompute UI to match invoice.
maria-cs: Customer wants a clear explanation and a one-time credit if invoice is correct but UI was wrong. They flagged this as urgent for month-end close.
ben-ops: Action items: 1) run recompute for 2026-04-28..2026-04-30: ```python tools/recompute_rollups.py --acct acct_42 --from 2026-04-28 --to 2026-04-30 --force``` 2) invalidate UI cache: ```curl -XPOST https://console.internal/api/cache/invalidate -d '{"acct":"acct_42","scope":"dashboard"}'```
raj-billing: I've started a background job to re-run ledger -> rollup join for that account. Job id job_98421. ETA ~ 18 minutes. I'll post logs when done.
alisa-sre: Also filing a reliability ticket to fix dedupe rules: legacy format vs canonical id handling. If the aggregator sees canonical ids, it shouldn't drop retries. Ticket RLY-2112.
ken-finance: For transparency we should offer the customer a one-time goodwill credit equivalent to the delta if they prefer refund. Delta tokens = invoice(35,210) - dashboard(28,134) => 7,076 tokens. I'll draft a credit note but will wait for confirmed recompute first.
billing-bot: Invoice INV-2026-04-ACME already processed. No automatic refund. Please escalate to finance for manual credit if approved.
raj-billing: job_98421 finished. Recomputed rollups show total tokens now 35,208 (off by 2 due to rounding on a micro-batch). Rollup export attached.
ben-ops: Invalidated UI cache and pushed new rollup snapshot. Dashboard now shows 35,208 tokens for acct_42. :white_check_mark:
maria-cs: Passed to customer: "We found a dashboard ingestion gap caused by a legacy dedupe mismatch; invoice was calculated from raw meter data and is correct. We have recomputed your dashboard totals and pushed a UI update. If you'd like a goodwill credit for the small 2-token rounding delta, we can issue one"
ken-finance: I'll hold credit in review. If customer requests, we'll issue a token credit for 2, or convert to dollar amount if they prefer.
maria-cs: Customer replied — they appreciate the clarity and want a one-time $0.02 credit for paperwork. Approved.
ken-finance: Credit created CR-1629 for $0.02 applied to account.
maria-cs: Closing ticket after sending summary email. Marking thread resolved. :tada:
